entities.name: 1762 Arakan earthquake
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary: The 1762 Arakan earthquake occurred at about 17:00 local time on 2 April, with an epicentre somewhere along the coast from Chittagong to Arakan in modern Myanmar. It had an estimated moment magnitude between 8.5 and 8.8 and a maximum estimated intensity of XI (Extreme). It triggered a local tsunami in the Bay of Bengal and caused at least 200 deaths. The earthquake was associated with major areas of both uplift and subsidence. It is also associated with a change in the course of the Brahmaputra River from east of Dhaka to 150 kilometres (93 mi) to the west via the Jamuna River. 1762 Arakan earthquake was a disaster (1762). Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.
